tools.name: file_document
tools.description: List unsaved native drafts and retained recovery with operation:list-dirty, optional exact project, bounded limit and nextCursor. Listing needs no target or open tab and returns stable IDs, revisions, kinds and recovery states. Inspect each returned target before saving or explicitly discarding; Save All never restores an unaccepted recovery. Inspect native file-backed working copies and use their declared typed edit, undo, save and recovery commands. Text/code, CSV/TSV, sequence and notebook adapters share the same owner with human views. Other scientific formats declare their supported owner and capabilities. Use target.path for an exact project-qualified or admitted absolute path, or target.documentId returned by inspect. The legacy tabId locator remains accepted for an ordinary text/table view. Inspect first and pass expectedRevision on changes. For text edits prefer operation:replace-string with oldText copied exactly from inspect.text and newText. The native owner finds the position; exactly one match is required, otherwise no edit is applied. Use inspect again for a missing match or include surrounding text for multiple matches. Use save afterward to publish the edited revision. Text offsets are zero-based UTF-16 positions in inspected LF-normalized text. Table indices are zero-based source body rows and columns; headers are column labels. CSV/TSV store values without rich formatting. Scientific operations preserve their own schemas and coordinates. Save publishes its captured revision and retains later edits. External disk changes refuse overwrite. Binary, sliced and readonly previews are not editable as ordinary text.

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: Read authorized registered authoring projects, reference folders, displayed folders, tabs and current caller capabilities. Choose notebook and design destinations from projects; pinned referenceFolders are sources, not authoring destinations. Displayed folders and the current selection do not define project access. DNAForge is the connected molecular-biology workspace. For primer or plasmid design and protocol-notebook requests, start with get_workspace.projects and inspect existing sequences using list_files, find_features and get_sequence. Deliver native editable assembly drafts, canonical saved oligos with bindings, and a native notebook. Preserve drafts until separately finalized. Choose an exact destination project; pinned reference folders are sources. Inspect available source sequences before calling them unknown or leaving their inspection for future work. Build requested construct variants with create_design, add_design_region and draft_design_assembly. Save the requested notebook in DNAForge rather than an unrelated repository. Persist every selected oligo that the plan instructs the user to order. Register the primers of a draft assembly with save_design_primers, which saves or links them and records the link on the design; never retype them through create_primer. For other oligos use save_designed_primer for a pinned design_primers candidate, or create_primer for exact authored notation, with annealingLength whenever the oligo has a 5-prime tail. Store each oligo's full ordered bases, modifications, annealing portion and relevant bindings, then read it back with get_primer. Text, CSV, sequence annotations and reference records do not create oligos. Do not write separate CSV or JSON copies of primers or of the design; exports are generated on request. Choose the destination project explicitly when a template belongs to another project. Create or update the protocol with the native notebook tools, structured tables and returned typed references to sources, exact regions, drafts and saved oligos or bindings. Use declared coordinate systems. Use get_entity_link for external hyperlinks and shell opens; use returned inline links or notebook reference payloads on their supported surfaces. Reuse existing identities on retry and respect saved revisions and unsaved edits. If a required operation is unavailable or refused, retain valid drafts and report the incomplete step without substituting another artifact type. An explanation alone does not authorize authoring. Background tool requests must preserve operating-system focus.

designId.description: Golden Gate design id returned by get_design, or waypoint://design/{id} URI.

expectedDesignVersion.description: Exact design version last read from get_design. Stale writes are refused.

schemaId.description: Schema id returned by list_moclo_schemas. No recipe is needed.

recipeId.description: Legacy recipe id; use schemaId for new calls.

stageId.description: Legacy stage id, paired with recipeId.

designId.description: Golden Gate design id returned by get_design, or waypoint://design/{id} URI.

slotId.description: Schema slot id returned by list_moclo_schemas.

query.description: Optional name, kit, part-type, ontology-role, or overhang search text.

partType.description: Optional exact biological part-type label. Overhang compatibility remains primary.

includePhysicallyIncompatible.description: Include digest fragments whose physical overhangs do not fit this slot.

tools.name: virtual_digest
tools.description: Run a virtual restriction digest on a sequence file and return the fragments, with cut-side-oriented ends, Golden Gate classification, internal-site flags, and a content-addressed digest snapshot id.

documentId.description: Stable sequence document ID or waypoint://sequence/{documentId} URI.

enzymes.description: Restriction enzyme names, e.g. ["BsaI"] or ["EcoRI","BamHI"]. Golden Gate classification (insert/backbone/unusable) is only computed for a SINGLE Type IIS enzyme — a two-enzyme digest returns ggType "rd" for every fragment.

tools.name: place_digest_fragment
tools.description: Place a virtual-digest fragment into an assembly SLOT. Requires the target slot id and the occupantFingerprint you last saw on it, for every mode, so you can never destroy contents you have not looked at.

designId.description: Design id, or a waypoint://design/{id} URI.

documentId.description: The stable sequence document ID — the SAME ID you passed to virtual_digest.

enzymes.description: The SAME enzyme list you passed to virtual_digest.

digestSnapshotId.description: The digestSnapshotId returned by virtual_digest. The digest is recomputed and refused if it no longer matches, which is how an edit to the source between your read and this write is caught instead of silently swapping which fragment you get.

fragmentCandidateId.description: The fragmentCandidateId of the fragment you chose. Never an ordinal index.

idempotencyKey.description: A caller-generated key for this placement intent. Retrying the same inputs with the same key returns a noop with existingRegionId instead of placing a duplicate. Reusing the key for different inputs is refused.

mode.description: fill_empty = put it in an EMPTY slot (refused if the slot is occupied). replace = overwrite an OCCUPIED slot, destroying what is there. insert_after / insert_before = create a NEW slot next to the target. There is no default: replacing is always an explicit choice.

targetRegionId.description: The slot to fill or replace, or the slot to insert next to. Read it from get_design.slots.

expectedSlotFingerprint.description: The occupantFingerprint of targetRegionId as you last saw it in get_design. Required for EVERY mode. If it no longer matches, the write is refused and the current slot map is returned — this is what makes it impossible to destroy something you have not looked at.

expectedDesignVersion.description: Design version you last read. Omit and no concurrency guard runs.

tools.name: set_primer_pbs_length
tools.description: Set the 3-prime annealing (primer binding site) length of an assembly primer.

designId.description: Design id returned by create_design, or a waypoint://design/{id} URI.

primerId.description: Stable id of the primer to edit, as returned by get_design / a previous call. Provide this OR both fragmentIndex and direction.

fragmentIndex.description: Zero-based index of the part (region) this primer amplifies, in the order the parts were added to the design. Must be paired with direction. Ignored if primerId is given and both agree.

direction.description: Which primer of the part's PCR pair: 'forward' anneals to the top strand at the part's 5' end, 'reverse' anneals to the bottom strand at its 3' end. Must be paired with fragmentIndex.

length.description: New primer-binding-site length in bases (bp), bounded by the template the primer's part provides; a refusal reports the allowed range as validLengthRange. This is the annealing length only — the 5′ tail is not counted and is not changed.

expectedDesignVersion.description: The design version you last read. If supplied and the design has moved on, the write is refused with code stale-design-version instead of overwriting. If omitted NO concurrency guard runs — the result reports versionGuardApplied so you can tell.

tools.name: set_primer_overhang_length
tools.description: Set the full 5-prime overhang (homology tail) length of an assembly primer. Gibson/NEBuilder only.

designId.description: Design id returned by create_design, or a waypoint://design/{id} URI.

primerId.description: Address the primer directly by its stable id. Ids are returned by this tool and by the assembly workbench. Provide this OR both fragmentIndex and direction.

fragmentIndex.description: Which part the primer amplifies, 0-based, in the order get_design lists regions. Must be paired with direction.

direction.description: Which primer of the fragment pair. The forward primer carries the tail for the junction BEFORE the part; the reverse primer carries the tail for the junction AFTER it. Must be paired with fragmentIndex.

length.description: New FULL synthesized 5' tail length in base pairs, 0..60. This includes any spacer cargo carried in the tail. 0 removes the tail entirely, leaving a plain PCR primer with no homology arm.

expectedDesignVersion.description: The design version you last read. If supplied and the design has moved on, the write is refused with code stale-design-version instead of overwriting. If omitted NO concurrency guard runs — the result reports versionGuardApplied so you can tell.

tools.name: set_golden_gate_offset
tools.description: Move the 4bp Golden Gate overhang along the sequence at a junction. Changes the oligos ordered, not the product.

designId.description: Design id returned by create_design, or a waypoint://design/{id} URI.

junctionIndex.description: Which junction to move. Junction i is the junction AFTER region i. Designs are circular, so a design with N parts has N junctions (the last one wraps). Provide this OR junctionId; if you provide both they must agree.

junctionId.description: Stable junction id, as returned in this tool's `junctions` array. Survives renumbering when parts are reordered, unlike junctionIndex.

offset.description: Where the overhang window sits, in BASE PAIRS relative to centred. 0 = centred on the junction (half the overhang taken from each part). Negative moves the window into the LEFT part, positive into the RIGHT part. Bounded by the design's offset limit (default 24 bp either way); a refusal reports the actual limit.

expectedDesignVersion.description: The design version you last read. If supplied and the design has moved on, the write is refused with code stale-design-version instead of overwriting. If omitted NO concurrency guard runs — the result reports versionGuardApplied so you can tell.

tools.name: set_pcr_polymerase
tools.description: Set the per-design PCR polymerase and Tm model used for its assembly primers; existing Tm verification is invalidated and refreshed.

designId.description: Design id returned by create_design, or a waypoint://design/{id} URI.

polymerase.description: Polymerase family, when the exact buffer does not matter. Resolves to that family's standard product: q5 -> q5-0 (NEB Q5); phusion -> phusion-0 (NEB Phusion (HF)); onetaq -> onetaq-0 (NEB OneTaq); taq -> taq-0 (NEB Taq); longamp -> lataq-0 (NEB LongAmp Taq). The result reports which product it resolved to and what else that family offers, so a GC-buffer variant is one follow-up call away. Provide this OR prodcode OR clear.

prodcode.description: Exact NEB product code, when the buffer matters (GC buffer and Hot Start variants have their own Tm behavior): q5-0 = NEB Q5; q5hs-0 = NEB Q5 Hot Start; phusion-0 = NEB Phusion (HF); phusion-1 = NEB Phusion (GC); onetaq-0 = NEB OneTaq; onetaq-1 = NEB OneTaq (GC); taq-0 = NEB Taq; hstaq-0 = NEB Hot Start Taq; lataq-0 = NEB LongAmp Taq. Provide this OR polymerase OR clear. If you pass both prodcode and polymerase they must agree.

clear.description: Pass true to remove the design-level polymerase, so primer Tm falls back to the app-wide setting (see get_primer_tm_config). Cannot be combined with polymerase or prodcode.

expectedDesignVersion.description: The design version you last read. If supplied and the design has moved on, the write is refused with code stale-design-version instead of overwriting. If omitted NO concurrency guard runs — the result reports versionGuardApplied so you can tell.

tools.name: remove_design_region
tools.description: Remove an assembly slot after proving knowledge of its current contents with the occupant fingerprint returned by get_design.

designId.description: Design id returned by create_design, or a waypoint://design/{id} URI.

regionId.description: The slot to remove, addressed by the `regionId` shown in get_design.slots. Never an ordinal position — positions are renumbered by every edit.

expectedSlotFingerprint.description: The `occupantFingerprint` of that slot exactly as get_design.slots reported it. REQUIRED. It hashes the slot CONTENT, and a slot keeps its id when it is cleared or refilled, so the id alone cannot prove you know what you are deleting. If it no longer matches, the removal is refused with SLOT_CHANGED and the current slot map is returned.

expectedDesignVersion.description: The design `version` you last read. If it has moved on, the removal is refused with stale-design-version instead of applying to a design you have not seen. Omitting it does NOT disable the guard — the version read at call time is still used, so a concurrent edit cannot slip in. `versionGuardApplied` reports whether YOU supplied one.

tools.name: reorder_design_regions
tools.description: Replace the complete assembly part order with an exact permutation of the region ids returned by get_design.

designId.description: Design id returned by create_design, or a waypoint://design/{id} URI.

order.description: The COMPLETE new left-to-right order of the assembly, as region ids. It must be a permutation of exactly the ids currently in the design: every current id present, exactly once, and nothing else. Read them from get_design.slots[].regionId. This is a full ordering, not a move instruction — there is no "move part X to position 3".

expectedDesignVersion.description: The design `version` you last read. Strongly recommended here: the ids can still be a valid permutation after someone has replaced what is INSIDE one of those slots, and only the version guard catches that. If it has moved on, the reorder is refused with stale-design-version. `versionGuardApplied` reports whether you supplied one.

tools.name: plan_overhang_optimization
tools.description: Rank Golden Gate overhang combinations against the bundled empirical ligation-fidelity dataset without changing the design.

designId.description: Design id returned by create_design, or a waypoint://design/{id} URI.

junctionIndex.description: Optional. Restrict the search to ONE junction, leaving every other junction exactly where it is. Junction i is the junction AFTER region i; a circular design with N parts has N junctions (the last one wraps). Omit to consider every movable junction at once, which is almost always what you want — overhangs cross-react as a SET, so the best single-junction move is often not part of the best set. If you pass this, you must pass the same value to apply_overhang_optimization.

tools.name: apply_overhang_optimization
tools.description: Apply one rank returned by plan_overhang_optimization after verifying that its proof-carrying plan id still names the same ranked options.

designId.description: Design id, or a waypoint://design/{id} URI. The same design you planned.

planId.description: The planId returned by plan_overhang_optimization. It is recomputed here and the write is refused if it no longer matches, which is how a design edit between your read and this write is caught instead of silently applying whatever now sits at that rank. You cannot obtain a planId without having looked at the ranked options, so no blind call can move an overhang.

rank.description: Which ranked combination to apply, as printed by plan_overhang_optimization. Rank 0 is the design exactly as it stands, so applying it changes nothing and returns noop. Ranks are only meaningful together with the planId they came from.

junctionIndex.description: Must be the SAME scope you passed to plan_overhang_optimization (omitted there means omitted here). The scope is part of the plan identity, so a mismatch is refused as a stale plan rather than applied to the wrong junction set.

expectedDesignVersion.description: The design version you last read. If supplied and the design has moved on, the write is refused with code stale-design-version. Independent of the planId guard: planId protects the MEANING of the rank, this protects against any concurrent edit at all. If omitted, the commit is still guarded against edits that race this call by the version read at call time, but no caller-supplied historical version is checked. `versionGuardApplied` reports whether YOU supplied one.

tools.name: create_reference
tools.description: Create a durable clickable reference to a whole sequence document or a rich DNAForge entity or selection. For a whole sequence document, use entityType:"sequence" with the stable documentId returned by workspace tools; do not link its physical path or resourceUri as a workspace file. For an ordinary non-sequence workspace file or folder, link its path inline instead. Identity is mandatory: sequence_region requires deepLinkParams.start/end (1-indexed inclusive), primer uses a validated canonical Registry oligo, including a standalone unbound oligo, with bindingId optional for a saved attachment; annotation requires top-level featureName or deepLinkParams.featureName. For an attached structure selection returned unchanged, reuse its authoritative refId with selection.kind="existing_reference" instead of copying residues or depending on a mounted viewer. Returns a referenceId; the app renders the chip from the completed tool result.

displayLabel.description: Short label for the reference chip (e.g., "pUC19", "GFP_F1")

documentId.description: Stable package/catalog identity for sequence, sequence_region, or annotation references. For a whole sequence only, a bare filename is accepted when it identifies exactly one currently open sequence tab; physical paths remain forbidden.

primerId.description: Existing canonical Registry oligo ID returned as registryEntityId by create_primer. Standalone unbound oligos are valid. Legacy library IDs are accepted only after explicit translation and verification.

bindingId.description: Optional existing primer attachment ID returned by get_primer. Omit to reference the oligo itself.

workspace.description: Exact mounted source project name or root for a primer artifact when ownership is ambiguous.

filePath.description: For non-sequence file-based entities: project-relative path from list_files. For a whole sequence only, a bare filename is accepted when it identifies exactly one currently open sequence tab. (e.g., "data/cas9-validation/file.gb"). Auto-constructs locator and validates the file exists.

locator.description: For non-file entities: entity://type/id URI. Use filePath instead for file-based entities.

start.description: 1-indexed inclusive region start

end.description: 1-indexed inclusive region end

wraps.description: True only when a circular region crosses the origin

deepLinkParams.description: Type-specific params for navigating to a specific state in the viewer. For sequence_region: { start: number, end: number, wraps?: boolean } (1-indexed positions, GenBank convention). For annotation: { featureName: string }; the app resolves the exact start/end from the file. Uses real minimap2 and bcftools pileup, preserves every read in accounting, reference topology, exact thresholds, coverage and source hashes. Inspect original read metadata, lengths and quality before selecting a preset; if technology is unknown, retain the choice as an exploratory assumption. Returns a job identity promptly and a complete get_ngs_analysis continuation. Copy continuation.arguments exactly, including documentId, operationId and name, to observe the job and open its completed candidate review. Requires installed minimap2, samtools and bcftools.

Inspect original headers and read length/quality distributions with your own script before selecting. A filename or read length alone does not establish sequencing technology. If technology is unknown, describe and retain the selected preset as an exploratory assumption.

An unknown identity is a lookup refusal, not evidence that the admitted analysis failed. When complete, persists read accounting, coverage, exact parameters and hashes plus candidate alleles. Each returned call includes proteinContext from current coding annotations: mapped reports the protein and single-allele consequence and includes complete inspection.arguments for inspect_variant_call, unavailable explains the limitation. Copy those arguments exactly. This does not establish available structure coordinates. Returns analysisId, a bounded first page and explicit continuation arguments for get_variant_analysis pagination. For a requested DNA position, call get_variant_analysis with start and end both equal to that position; do not parse a spilled result file with shell tools. All calls remain available through native pagination; color_variant_protein uses that exact analysisId. Failed/incomplete jobs are not evidence.

tools.name: mol_show_interaction_context
tools.description: Construct standard native Molstar contacts for chosen physical molecules or residues in an existing structure view. focus:true (default) reframes the new context in the current view direction; focus:false preserves the current native camera pose, including after an earlier focused context is replaced. For every new protein interface, explicitly provide BOTH interfaceDetailSide:target|partner|both and interfaceDetailBasis:contacts|burial from the question; missing or partial choices fail before rendering. Ligand, ion and RNA-only contexts do not require these choices, including ligand calls labeled interface because native ligand ownership takes priority. For a shared multi-structure view, use sceneStructureRef from mol_get_scene.structureIdentities and exact instance_id selections. The producer chooses one coherent deposited conformer and uses the fixed native 5 Å whole-residue discovery neighborhood and unchanged native provider settings. For a non-polymer binding target, including a single ion, show every calculated contact crossing from that target to its surroundings; for an interface, show every contact crossing targetSelection and partnerSelection. Internal contacts within either side are excluded from binding explanations. Other local residue-focus views retain the standard complete Focus neighborhood. Contact categories, radius and individual lines cannot be chosen by the agent. Every retained contact preserves its native classification, complete aromatic or charge-group features and standard guide geometry; coincident classifications share a physical guide. Native classification is coordinate inference, not proof of chemistry or binding energy. Build broad cartoon context first, then use this tool for the physical focus. For a complete ligand, atomic pocket detail includes every residue with native partner-induced surface burial, plus retained contact support and chemical attachments. Packing membership is independent of the enabled dotted-line categories; unrelated discovery-neighborhood residues are excluded. The complete molecular ligand always owns its binding contour, including when interface mode or the protein side is requested. Disconnected single-atom ions are binding targets but do not form a merged ligand envelope. Every declared ion remains visible independently of its dotted lines. All displayed same-species ion sites in the same deposited operator and contacting polymer unit envelope form one computed contact boundary. The native 5 Å neighborhood is recomputed around that complete cohort, with unchanged contact categories and distance settings, so choosing one discovery seed cannot omit the other displayed sites’ native guides. A protein interface requires surfaceSide:target|partner and partnerSelection. Its residue surface patch is computed from native solvent-accessible area lost when the declared partner is added, including nonpolymer groups, using fixed sampling. Complete native burial measurements on both sides are retained separately from atomic presentation. Choose interfaceDetailSide:target|partner|both and interfaceDetailBasis:contacts|burial from the question. Contacts selects supporting protein residues on the chosen side; burial also selects its complete buried-residue packing. Protein interfaces default to interfaceProteinAtomicMode:sidechain-with-trace, using Molstar's maintained selector to omit redundant protein backbone sticks while retaining every required native polar/aromatic/charge feature and actual deposited covalent path to the cartoon trace. Choose full-residue when backbone geometry explains the question. It refines protein depiction only; complete measurements, guides, contours, nonprotein chemistry and attachments are retained. Opposing required guide features remain opaque, including complete aromatic and charge groups and mandatory native chemical attachments. These are minimum guide-support atoms, not complete opposing side chains. There is no automatic protein-interface detail choice; archived saved views retain their recorded presentation. Mixed protein/glycan interfaces preserve nonprotein chemistry and complete glycan contours; ligand-binding, ion and RNA-only contexts retain existing detail. The chosen side supplies the surface geometry. surfaceExtent:complete displays its whole contour; contact-patch deliberately hides residues outside the computed patch. A side containing molecular ligands or attached glycans always keeps a complete contour; pure protein interfaces default to contact-patch and may explicitly request complete. Burial measurements remain separate from contour visibility. The patch is sampled residue coverage, not an exact atomic contact face or binding-energy estimate. Surface colors follow that side's identity. The viewer-bound profile remains fixed, while styling, camera and numeric measurement labels remain editable. Later scene edits must retain the complete generated contact group. Reinvoking this tool explicitly recomputes the current step instead of stacking another group. Inspect the native readback and final image before saving.

Keep the deposited component and empty measurement when an encoded position has no atoms. publish takes all data inside publication. Example: {operation:"publish",structureViewId,publication:{id:"my-data",name:"My results",source:{label:"Python output",script:"analysis.py"},table:{format:"csv",path:"results.csv",sha256:outputDigest},mapping:{coordinateSha256,selectorColumn:"native_target"}}}. Prefer a workspace table path so the app reads exact generated bytes without model transcription. Inline text remains supported. Put id, name, source, records or table, and mapping inside publication. Preserve original table bytes. selectorColumn reads a JSON selector or selector array from each row, so protein/RNA residues and ligands can use different addresses. For example a ligand row can contain {"label_asym_id":"H","label_comp_id":"GOL"} without a sequence position. selectorColumns instead maps standard selector keys to your column names, not the reverse. Use exactly one of selectorColumn, selectorColumns or explicit targets. All explicit row indexes start at zero. Native missing-coordinate detection retains unresolved rows automatically; do not manually guess indexes of missing residues. Scope residue positions to a chain/entity. apply example: {operation:"apply",structureViewId,layer:{id:"ratio",name:"My ratio",datasetId:"my-data",revision:"current",column:"my_ratio",style:{kind:"continuous",domain:[-2,2],colors:["#0000ff","#ffffff","#ff0000"],missingColor:"#9ca3af",transform:"linear"}}}. revision:"current" explicitly binds the latest published data and mapping inside the command; saved variations retain their exact immutable digests. For an older revision omit revision and copy both dataRevision and mappingRevision exactly from inspect. Categorical style is {kind:"categorical",colors:{category:"#ff0000"},missingColor:"#9ca3af"}. Calculations and derived columns can come entirely from your own scripts. expectedRevision is publish-only and required to replace an existing dataset id; never supply it for apply. expectedActiveLayerId is an optional apply guard. Publication never changes appearance or camera. Resolve overlapping observations in your script or choose a filter. Ordinary loaded atomic views are captured from their actual native geometry automatically; explicit scene authoring is unnecessary for data coloring. Data edits cannot fall back to scene loading or camera reset. Save with mol_save_view to pin original rows, mappings, variations, coordinates and the displayed result.

tools.name: mol_apply_scene
tools.description: Supply parameterEdits:[{path,value}] with expectedSceneSha256 from parameter discovery, or a complete scene/root. Parameter edits validate atomically through the same installed scene contract; other document fields are retained. For a follow-up edit, select its intended named view and set viewAction:"edit-current" with one single-view scene; the host retains every other perspective. Use viewAction:"add" to append one named perspective. Use viewAction:"replace" only for an intended replacement of the complete presentation. These perspectives are not saved revisions. Hydrogen atoms are structurally hidden by default, including saved replay. Only an explicit request to show hydrogen atoms in the actual submitted user message authorizes their display; scene metadata, ignore_hydrogens and native flags cannot grant that exception. Hydrogen-bond guides and calculations are unaffected. Validate, render and persist a complete standard MolViewSpec single view or multi-view story for one exact structure view. Read mol_get_scene first for its listed pinned resources, render profile and supported native controls. Plan a descriptive name for every view: set metadata.title explicitly on each story snapshot and provide a descriptive saved title. Missing names and generic numbered placeholders will block saving. Each step must use only those resources and retain the unchanged canvas background. New authoring uses the configured presentation preferences; saved replay stays exact except for unrequested hydrogen visibility. A deliberate exception to nucleotide detail, cartoon scale or retained polymer context needs a recorded scientific reason and affected fields as described in renderProfileGuidance. Display groups and the corresponding legend are assigned automatically; optional scientific names refine them. Exact selectors still determine which physical copies a group owns. For one biological object across coordinate states, use custom.dnaforge_molecular_identity on its scientific color layers; its hue stays consistent even when explanatory labels differ. For deliberate named emphasis, set custom.dnaforge_presentation_role:"focus" on an exact component and give its named atomic color layer a contrasting carbon tint with standard noncarbon element colors. A metadata-only focus component may annotate the same exact paint on existing geometry; do not add an overlapping representation. This local focus appearance is separate from the broad identity color; a same-hue named focus inside broader atomic/cartoon context fails before mutation. Retain corresponding focus appearance across compared states. Retain each complete native-interaction-context-v1 primitives group from the current scene in a relevant detail step: silently dropping, hiding or changing computed contact endpoints fails with MVS_INTERACTION_CONTACTS_LOST before mutation. Contact guides are constructed only by mol_show_interaction_context; hand-picked tubes, atom lines and fabricated contact metadata are rejected. Complete existing sets may be styled; neutral distance measurements and narrative arrows remain supported. Duplicate geometry and missing required attachment bonds return factual errors. An unchanged display tree fails unless reapplyUnchanged deliberately restores a drifted view. Success confirms rendering and persistence; assess scientific clarity with the readback and screenshot before saving. Use multiple complementary views when they make the explanation clearer, such as an overview plus a close-up or views of different states. Choose overview, registered comparison and detail for the evidence each provides. Frame the complete functional unit; retain needed whole-object context in a companion to local focus. Use surfaces for shape claims and distinguish whole contours from contact patches. Protein interfaces default to native sidechain-with-trace; choose full-residue for backbone claims. Start local framing with native focus, then inspect the preview. For named emphasis, mark an exact component custom.dnaforge_presentation_role:"focus" and use a contrasting carbon tint with standard element colors; this can annotate existing atomic paint without new geometry. Preserve corresponding identities and emphasis. Align justified regions, share orientation/scale exposing deciding features, resolve occlusion and explain scope changes. Add atoms/guides only to explain the question.

tools.name: save_design_primers
tools.description: Register a draft assembly's primers as saved oligos, or link each one to the identical oligo already saved in the same project (exact bases and chemistry), and record on the design which saved oligo and revision each primer uses. Each primer's binding part, 5-prime tail, part, direction and source site stay with the design. The call creates no source attachments, never finalizes, is safe to repeat, and reports several identical saved oligos as ambiguous instead of guessing; settle those with choices. restoreMissingBindingSplit records the binding and tail split on a linked oligo that lacks one. Do not retype assembly primers through create_primer. Use get_design to read the current version and primer IDs.

designId.description: Design id or waypoint://design/<id>.

expectedDesignVersion.description: Design version last returned by get_design.

saveUnsaved.description: Register primers that have no identical saved oligo. Defaults to true; false links existing oligos and reports the rest.

restoreMissingBindingSplit.description: Record the binding and tail split on linked or matched oligos that have none. Defaults to false.

choices.description: Saved oligo to use for each primer reported as ambiguous.

tools.name: create_strain
tools.description: Save a planned strain with genotype, selections, ancestry and exact sequence links through the native strain writer. Enrolled projects accept database history before file delivery and Registry/Git publication; this never claims a physical strain was constructed.

workspace.description: Project name; required when multiple projects are open.

strainId.description: Stable identity for an unchanged retry; otherwise allocated by the writer.

fields.description: Registry fields. genotypeCanonical is required; species, markers, growthConditions and notes are supported. These describe intended designs, not measured results.

targetEntityId.description: Existing parent strain or sequence identity, never a path.

targetRevisionId.description: Exact accepted target revision. Omit only to pin the target accepted at creation time.

relationships.description: Planned links owned by the new strain: derives_from points to its parent; has_genome to an exact chromosome/allele; carried_by identifies a plasmid carried by the strain. Save the exact intended sequences first.

tools.name: list_scientific_objects
tools.description: List accepted scientific identities, paths and exact revision pins in an open project without sequence bases or working-file reads. Unenrolled projects return enrolled:false.
